analysis.title: Capital Market Outlook, November 9, 2026
key_insights: CIO says the U.S. is following the typical midterm-year pattern: GDP growth accelerated through 2026 (Q3 peak of 3.4%), earnings momentum peaked, and the market is now pricing the slowdown from that peak. P/E compression reflects the coming deceleration in earnings growth.

Slower but still healthy profit growth is expected to support the bull market in 2027. Policy moves from maximum accommodation to a midcycle balance, which the CIO says should prevent overheating without needing overly restrictive policy.
Historically the S&P 500 has corrected about 20% ahead of midterms and then risen about 30% from the bottom in the following year.

Q3 2026 GDP: consumer spending growth averaged 3.8% over the past six months, AI investment grew at a midteens rate, and private sector purchases grew just under 5%. Imports of Asia-made technology gear for the AI buildout subtract from headline GDP.

Analyst earnings revisions have started to roll over, so the rate of earnings growth is likely to slow. The CIO says the second derivative of growth has turned negative, but moving from far above trend to trend growth is still enough for the bull market to continue.

The Fed moved from rate cuts to rate hikes in 2026 under Chair Warsh. Spreads on weaker balance-sheet borrowers have widened, and the CIO says the damage is so far confined to the lowest-quality borrowers and it is early in a new credit cycle.

Ned Davis Research: the S&P 500 has gained an average of 4.4% in the first year of postwar tightening cycles. Aggressive cycles averaged a 3.6% decline a year later and gradual cycles a 10.5% gain. The market appears to price hikes in December and March, and the CIO sees low odds of an aggressive cycle given benign wage pressure and strong productivity.

Tariffs have cut U.S. imports from China from about 20% of the total ten years ago to under 10% (Strategas), but overall trade has kept growing with the global economy. The CIO calls this reglobalization into new trade spheres rather than deglobalization.

McKinsey: U.S. and China companies hold about 90% of the market value in 18 growth arenas. U.S. companies hold 75% of the market cap and generate about 50% of revenues. The CIO uses this to argue the U.S. valuation premium persists and that new technologies carry higher margins, supporting a higher earnings trajectory.

The midterm results showed sentiment against rapid AI data center buildout, and beneficiaries are being revalued for slower growth. Disapproval of the Iran War also showed in the results, and energy prices fell on hopes of a quicker end to the war, which lowered inflation expectations and rates.

Equity indexes sold off Thursday, November 5 on concern that a Democratic sweep could add short-term policy uncertainty around the AI buildout, deficits and oil. The CIO would use weakness in Equities and Fixed Income to rebalance for 2027.
CIO sees conditions building for a year-end rally and calls the recent sharp declines in Financials, parts of Industrials, higher-quality semiconductors and power generation potentially overdone.
With the 10-year Treasury yield near 5% and real yields above 2.5%, the CIO favors moving out of cash and the front end of the curve to extend duration.

AI capex: the 15 largest data center developers are expected to spend over $1.4 trillion in 2027, 3.5% to 4% of U.S. GDP. About 34GW of IT capacity is under construction, about 70% in the U.S. (BloombergNEF).

AI financing: highest-rated data center bond yields rose from below 5% at the start of the year to about 7%, and AI-linked firms have raised over $460B of debt this year, more than double 2025. The 15 largest listed data center companies would need $2.5 trillion of revenue in 2032 to earn their cost of capital, about 5 times expected 2026 revenue.

The CIO says wider credit spreads and higher yields reflect a financing shortage for the buildout, which it calls a natural development. It believes the AI buildout is closer to the middle than the end and sees weakness in higher-quality AI-chain names as a buying opportunity. It is watching builder balance sheets, margins and order backlogs or cancellations.

China's WTO accession (25th anniversary in December 2026): the CIO argues the West has become more like China through tariffs, chip subsidies, industrial policy and investment screening, and that returns now depend on geopolitics, energy costs, protectionism and national security as well as earnings and valuations.

China is about 28% of global manufacturing (World Bank) versus 17% for the U.S., its export share rose from 4% in 2001 to 15%, and it is on course for a merchandise trade surplus above $1 trillion. The CIO expects China to keep relying on exports and investment amid weak domestic demand, which keeps it neutral on Europe given Germany's exposure.

earnings_insights: Profit growth followed the stronger 2026 GDP higher and has peaked in momentum. Analyst earnings revisions have started to roll over, and the CIO expects slower but still positive earnings growth in 2027.
The CIO expects higher-quality, less leveraged segments to outperform as financial conditions tighten and earnings momentum slows.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Peak of growth acceleration through the first three quarters of 2026, with growth expected to slow in 2027 as fiscal support fades.

Core inflation is forecast to edge up in 2027 while headline falls.
BofA baseline implies further hikes. Q3 2026 actual was 3.88%, and the market is described as pricing hikes in December and March.
Real yields above 2.5% are cited as offering attractive income, and the CIO favors extending duration.

trade_ideas.description: Move out of cash and the front end of the curve to extend duration, given 10-year yields near 5% and real yields above 2.5%
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher yields may offer attractive income potential.

trade_ideas.description: Use weakness in higher-quality segments of the AI chain (including higher-quality semiconductors) as a buying opportunity for investors underexposed to them
trade_ideas.rationale: The CIO says the AI buildout is closer to the middle than the end and that financing-driven weakness is a natural part of the cycle.
trade_ideas.risk: Builder balance sheet strain, lower profitability and margins, and order backlogs or cancellations.

trade_ideas.description: Use weakness in Equities and Fixed Income to rebalance and reposition portfolios for 2027, including the oversold parts of Financials, Industrials, semiconductors and power generation
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth, margins and productivity remain supportive and volatility should settle.

risk_factors: An aggressive Fed tightening cycle: Ned Davis data show aggressive cycles averaged a 3.6% S&P 500 decline a year later.
Fading fiscal stimulus and slowing earnings growth in 2027, with the second derivative of growth already negative.
Credit stress spreading from the lowest-quality borrowers as financial conditions tighten, in what the CIO calls a new credit cycle.
AI buildout financing: not enough capital to fund the buildout, wider credit spreads, $460B of AI-linked debt raised this year, and $2.5 trillion of 2032 revenue needed to earn the cost of capital.
Policy uncertainty from the midterms around the AI buildout, deficits and oil, plus political sentiment to slow data center construction.
China's export dependence and the exposure of manufacturing-heavy economies such as Germany.
charts_described: Exhibit 1A and 1B plot China's share of global manufacturing value-add and share of world exports. The text gives China at about 28% of global manufacturing and a 15% export share, up from 4% in 2001.
Exhibits 2A and 2B plot hyperscaler AI investment growth against revenue growth and rising debt issuance among major hyperscalers. The text gives no values for either chart.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility rose around the November 5 sell-off. The CIO expects volatility to start settling and sees conditions building for a year-end rally as focus shifts from uncertainty and rotation to growth, margins and productivity.
Week ended 11/06 total returns: Nasdaq -3.4%, S&P 500 -2.7%, MSCI Emerging Markets -4.1%, WTI crude -12.8%, Bloomberg Commodity -4.5%, gold spot +5.1%.
geopolitical: Iran War: midterm results registered disapproval, and energy prices fell on hopes for a quicker end to the war, lowering inflation expectations and rates.
U.S.-China trade: tariffs cut U.S. imports from China from about 20% to under 10% of the total (Strategas), with overall trade still growing.
China's WTO accession anniversary: Western governments adopting subsidies, tariffs, semiconductor support and investment screening, as China keeps a state-led economy under Xi Jinping.
Midterm election results: a Democratic sweep raised short-term policy uncertainty around the AI buildout, deficits and oil.

tension_points.theme: 2027 equity bull market versus Fed tightening
tension_points.bull_case: The CIO expects slower but healthy profit growth, benign wage pressure and strong productivity to support the bull market in 2027. The market appears to price only modest hikes in December and March, and gradual tightening cycles have averaged a 10.5% S&P 500 gain a year later.
tension_points.bear_case: Aggressive tightening cycles have averaged a 3.6% S&P 500 decline a year later (Ned Davis). The fiscal boost fades in 2027, earnings revisions are rolling over, and credit spreads are widening for weaker borrowers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation forcing the Fed into an aggressive tightening cycle rather than the modest December and March hikes the market prices.

tension_points.bull_case: The CIO says the buildout is closer to the middle than the end, and that wider credit spreads and higher yields are a natural development that makes weakness in higher-quality AI names a buying opportunity.
tension_points.bear_case: The 15 largest data center companies need $2.5 trillion of 2032 revenue to earn their cost of capital, about 5 times expected 2026 revenue. Top-rated data center bond yields rose from below 5% to about 7%, and capital providers may not be able to fund the buildout.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deterioration in builder balance sheets, profitability and margins, or rising order backlogs and cancellations.

theme_stances.key_argument: Midterm-year growth peaked and the market has priced the slowdown, which leaves slower but still healthy profit growth to support a bull market in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: setting the stage for continued economic expansion and an ongoing but more tempered bull market

theme_stances.key_argument: Financing concerns have widened credit spreads and lifted yields, but the CIO sees this as a natural part of the cycle and weakness in higher-quality AI names as a buying chance.
theme_stances.evidence: we still believe we are closer to the middle of the AI buildout than to the end

theme_stances.key_argument: With 10-year yields near 5% and real yields above 2.5%, the CIO favors moving out of cash and the front end to extend duration.
theme_stances.evidence: we favor moving out of cash and the front end of the curve to extend duration
